newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: E.Asia Oilseeds - Korea to pick up beans, soymeal.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - Korea to pick up beans, soymeal.

text.p: South Korea is expected to buy up to 40,000 tonnes of soybeans and 40,000 tonnes of soymeal for September/October arrival to take advantage of recent sharp falls in world prices, dealers said on Monday.
The National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) said it would invite tenders on Tuesday to buy 40,000 tonnes of soymeal for arrival between September 30-October 20.
The state-run Agricultural and Fishery Marketing Corp (AFMC) also said it would invite tenders on July 15 to buy 40,000 tonnes of No.1 soybean for September 20 to October 20 arrival.
One dealer said several feed millers had recently bought 10,400 tonnes of palm kernel meal from Nidera last week through private negotiation.

Some 5,200 tonnes were sold at US$85.29 a tonne C&F for August 16-September 5 shipment and the remaining 5,200 tonnes at $86 a tonne C&F for September 16-October 5 shipment to the ports of Inchon and Ulsan.

China, which recently bought 100,000 tonnes of soymeal and 50,000 tonnes of soybeans the past two weeks, is also expected to pick up an additional 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal if futures prices in Chicago continue to fall, dealers said.
"A total of two 50,000-tonne U.S. soymeal shipments were bought recently," said a Beijing-based Chinese buyer. "We also bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans last week."
All three shipments were for late October to mid-November delivery, he added.
Japanese oilseed buyers, however, are likely to remain sidelined this week, although some will buy for prompt shipment, traders said.
"We'll closely monitor weather condition in soybean growing areas in the U.S. from now on. But we have no urgent reason to buy now," a soybean trader in Tokyo said.
The buyers will continue to wait for lower-priced new U.S. soybean crop from around October, they said.
Japan's soybean crushing in May reached 318,628 tonnes, up 7.8 percent from a year earlier, the Agriculture Ministry said.
The country's output of soy oil during May reached 57,089 tonnes and that of soymeal 242,116 tonnes, it said.
